newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Creditanstalt supervisory board names Hampel new CEO.
newsitem.headline: Creditanstalt supervisory board names Hampel new CEO.

text.p: Austria's Creditanstalt said on Tuesday its supervisory board had voted career banker Erich Hampel to succeed Guido Schmidt-Chiari as the bank's chief executive.
"The new chief executive Erich Hampel will start in his position on May 15," the bank said in a statement.
Board member Alarich Fenyves, who has been in charge of the bank's international business, was named as Hampel's number two, Creditanstalt said.
Creditanstalt is controlled by Bank Austria, which acquired the state's majority stake in the bank in January. Bank Austria chief executive Gerhard Randa heads Creditanstalt's supervisory board.
Hampel, 47, currently chairs the board of postal savings bank PSK, which is due for partial privatisation this year.
Schmidt-Chiari was one of the most vociferous opponents of the sale of Creditanstalt to market leader Bank Austria. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 274
